info.title: Closedloop API
info.description: REST API for the Closedloop human-governed, AI-centric software delivery platform. Use this API to manage projects, workstreams, documents, artifacts, and comment threads. Requests require a Bearer API key with the prefix `sk_live_` unless an operation declares its own `security`; an operation that names `sessionAuth` accepts a signed-in Closedloop session, either as an alternative to an API key or in place of one. Read each operation's own `security`.

get.description: Returns a list of documents visible to the authenticated organization. Documents are typed artifacts: **PRD** (Product Requirements Document — describes what to build and why), **IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN** (step-by-step technical plan for executing a PRD), **FEATURE** (a feature specification), **TEMPLATE** (a reusable document template), or **DOC** (an evergreen document). Filter by `type` to fetch only plans, by `projectId` to scope to a project, or by `assigneeId` to fetch documents assigned to a specific user.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by document type. PRD = product requirements, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN = technical implementation plan, FEATURE = feature spec, TEMPLATE = reusable template, DOC = evergreen document. The `ISSUE` alias is also accepted and is treated as `FEATURE` (the product's "Issue" is a rename of Feature).

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Filter by project. Accepts a UUID or slug.

parameters.name: assigneeId
parameters.description: Filter by assignee user UUID.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by lifecycle status (ISS-6778), applied in the database so the result is narrowed before paging rather than after. **Repeated**, not comma-joined: `?status=TODO&status=IN_PROGRESS`, matched as `IN`. Accepted values are the union of both vocabularies — Documents (PRD, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, TEMPLATE, DOC) use `DocumentStatus`, Features/Issues use `IssueStatus`. The union is NOT narrowed by `type` — the stored column is freeform and off-vocabulary rows exist, so a combination the lifecycle forbids returns an empty result rather than a 400. An unknown value, a comma-joined one such as `status=TODO,IN_PROGRESS`, or a blank `status=`, is rejected with 400 rather than silently dropped. Omit to apply no status filter.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Optional page size (FEA-4373). Omit to return every matching document (the default). When supplied, bounds the result to this many rows, newest first (by createdAt, then id); accepted range 1-500. Pass alongside offset to page.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based offset for paging (FEA-4373). Only valid together with limit; an offset without a limit is rejected with 400.

parameters.name: includeTotal
parameters.description: Opt into the paged response envelope (ISS-4576). Omit (the default) to receive the bare `data` array of documents. Pass `true` to receive a `DocumentListPage` envelope under `data` instead — the page plus a real server-side `total` counted over the same filter, with `limit`, `offset`, and `hasMore`. `includeTotal=true` requires `limit`; without one it is rejected with 400 (the total-bearing read must be bounded).

200.description: List of documents. The `data` shape is selected by `includeTotal`: the bare document array by default, or a `DocumentListPage` envelope when `includeTotal=true`.

oneOf.description: Default response (`includeTotal` omitted): the bare array of matching documents.

data.description: A bare `Document[]` by default, or a `DocumentListPage` envelope when `includeTotal=true`.

400.description: Invalid query parameters.

post.summary: Create a document
post.description: Requires an API key with `write` scope. Creates a new document. The `type` field determines what kind of artifact is created: **PRD** captures product requirements, **IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN** is a detailed plan typically produced from a PRD, **FEATURE** captures a feature specification, **TEMPLATE** is a reusable document template, and **DOC** is an evergreen document. The `type` field also accepts the **ISSUE** alias, which is treated as **FEATURE** (the product's "Issue" is a rename of Feature). Whether the document lives inside a project depends on its `type`: the project-bound subtypes (**PRD**, **IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN**, **FEATURE**, and its **ISSUE** alias) **require** a `projectId`, a **DOC** may omit or carry a `projectId`, and a **TEMPLATE** must **omit** it — supplying one for a **TEMPLATE** is rejected with a 400. Provide initial `content` as a string (Markdown or plain text). The document is versioned automatically — each subsequent update creates a new version while preserving history. To link the new document to a parent PRD (for example, creating a plan that was produced by a PRD), pass the parent's ID as `sourceId`; the platform will create a PRODUCES artifact link automatically.

allOf.description: Fields common to both request variants. The body must additionally match exactly one of the variants below, which fix the allowed `type` values and the `projectId` requirement based on whether the document is project-bound or organization-level.

projectId.description: UUID or slug of the project this document belongs to. Conditionally required by `type`: **required** for the project-bound subtypes (**PRD**, **IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN**, **FEATURE**), optional for **DOC**, and must be **omitted** for **TEMPLATE** — supplying it for a **TEMPLATE** is rejected with a 400.

sourceId.description: Optional UUID or slug of an existing artifact that produced (generated) this document. Creates a PRODUCES artifact link automatically.

fileName.description: Optional file name to associate with the document.

content.description: Initial document content (Markdown or plain text).

status.description: Initial lifecycle status. The valid vocabulary depends on `type`: a FEATURE artifact uses the Features vocabulary (`IssueStatus`: TRIAGE, BACKLOG, TODO, ...), while every other type (PRD, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, TEMPLATE, DOC) uses the Documents vocabulary (`DocumentStatus`: DRAFT, IN_REVIEW, ...). A status outside the target type's vocabulary is rejected.

dueDate.description: Optional due date for the document. Accepts a date-only value (YYYY-MM-DD) or a timezone-qualified datetime.

assigneeId.description: UUID of the user to assign to this document.

approverId.description: UUID of the user designated to approve this document.

inlineImages.description: Optional inline images to embed in the document's initial content. Each image's `placeholder` token must appear in `content`; the server uploads the image as an attachment and rewrites the placeholder into a Markdown image reference. When supplied, the response includes `inlineImages` and the expanded `versionContent`.

placeholder.description: Unique token that appears verbatim in `content` and is replaced by the uploaded image's Markdown reference.

filename.description: File name to store the attachment under.

mimeType.description: MIME type of the image. Must match the decoded `dataBase64` payload.

altText.description: Optional alternative text for the image.

oneOf.title: Project-bound document (PRD, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, FEATURE)
oneOf.description: Create a document inside a project. These subtypes are project-scoped, so `projectId` is REQUIRED. Supplying an organization-level `type` here is invalid — use an organization-level variant instead.

type.description: Project-bound document subtype. Each of these is created inside a project and therefore requires `projectId`.

oneOf.title: Organization-level document (DOC)
oneOf.description: Create a document at the organization level. A DOC may omit or carry a `projectId`.

type.description: Organization-level document type. A DOC may omit or carry a `projectId`.

oneOf.title: Organization-level document (TEMPLATE)
oneOf.description: Create a document at the organization level. A TEMPLATE is org-scoped and must OMIT `projectId`; supplying one is rejected with a 400 (`projectId is not allowed for organization-level document types`).

type.description: Organization-level document type. A TEMPLATE is created at the org level and must omit `projectId`.

put.description: Requires an API key with `write` scope. Updates mutable fields on a document. All fields are optional — send only the fields you want to change. Updating `status` advances the document lifecycle (e.g., DRAFT → IN_REVIEW → APPROVED). Changing `assigneeId` sends an assignment notification to the new assignee. This endpoint does NOT update the document content; to write new content, use the document versions endpoint. When updating `status`, clients may pass `expectedStatus` with the value they previously read; the server returns HTTP 409 with code `stale_status` if the persisted status changed before the write, unless it already equals the `status` sent.

status.description: New lifecycle status. The valid vocabulary depends on the document's `type`: a FEATURE artifact uses the Features vocabulary (`IssueStatus`), while every other type uses the Documents vocabulary (`DocumentStatus`). A status outside the target artifact's vocabulary is rejected.

get.description: Returns links associated with the specified artifact. Links represent directional relationships between artifacts: **PRODUCES** means the source artifact generated or produced the target (e.g., a PRD PRODUCES an IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN), **BLOCKS** means the source is blocking progress on the target, **RELATES_TO** is a general non-hierarchical association. Use `direction` to control which end of the link the query artifact appears on: `source` returns links where the artifact is the source, `target` returns links where it is the target, `both` (default) returns all links regardless of direction. Use `mode=tree` with `maxDepth` to traverse multi-level dependency chains (e.g., PRD → PLAN → FEATUREs).

parameters.description: UUID or slug of the artifact to query links for.

parameters.name: linkType

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Which role the query artifact plays. `source` = artifact is the source of the link, `target` = artifact is the target, `both` = either role (default).

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Query mode. `direct` = only immediate links (default), `tree` = recursively traverse the link graph up to `maxDepth` levels.

parameters.name: maxDepth
parameters.description: Maximum depth when `mode=tree`. Range 1–50, default 10.

get.description: Returns tags in the authenticated organization. Tags are org-scoped labels that can be applied to artifacts and projects. Returns every tag by default; pass `limit`/`offset` to page, `search` to filter by substring, or `name` for an exact case-insensitive lookup. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Optional page size (ISS-7461). Omit to return every tag in the organization (the long-standing default other consumers rely on). When supplied, bounds the result to this many rows ordered by name; accepted range 1-100. Pass alongside offset to page.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based offset for paging (ISS-7461). Only valid together with limit; an offset without a limit is rejected with 400. Accepted range 0-10000.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the tag name. `%` and `_` are matched literally, not as pattern operators. Only valid together with limit; a search without a limit is rejected with 400, because the substring match is unindexed and would scan the whole organization.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Exact, case-insensitive name lookup; returns zero or one tag. Matched as `lower(name)` with NO trimming, the same way the `(organization_id, lower(name))` unique index compares, so a name with leading or trailing space is a DIFFERENT tag. Cannot be combined with limit, offset, or search — the combination is rejected with 400 rather than silently ignoring one of them. It MAY be combined with `includeTotal=true`, and a client that wants to know its filter was applied should do so: an older server that predates this parameter ignores it and returns the whole catalogue as a bare array, which a bare zero-or-one array is otherwise indistinguishable from.

parameters.name: includeTotal
parameters.description: Opt into the paged response envelope (ISS-7461). Omit (the default) to receive the bare `data` array of tags. Pass `true` to receive a `TagListPage` envelope under `data` instead — the page plus a real server-side `total` counted over the same filter, and `hasMore`. `includeTotal=true` requires `limit` OR `name`; with neither it is rejected with 400 (the total-bearing read must be bounded, and a `name` lookup is already bounded to one row by the `(organization_id, lower(name))` unique index). An explicit `includeTotal=false` is the same as omitting it: the unbounded bare array, never a truncated page.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Accepted and then IGNORED. Retained only so already-installed clients that still serialize it are not rejected by validation; there has never been a project-scoped tag predicate behind it. Sending it does not narrow the result set — do not present it as a filter.

200.description: Tags matching the query. The `data` shape is selected by `includeTotal`: the bare tag array by default, or a `TagListPage` envelope when `includeTotal=true`.

oneOf.description: Default response (`includeTotal` omitted): the bare array of matching tags.

data.description: A bare `Tag[]` by default, or a `TagListPage` envelope when `includeTotal=true`.

400.description: Invalid query parameters — an unknown param, an out-of-range bound, `offset` without `limit`, `search` without `limit`, `includeTotal` without `limit` or `name`, or `name` combined with `limit`/`offset`/`search`.

post.summary: Apply one tag to many artifacts with per-item results
post.description: Accepts an API key with `write` scope, or a signed-in Closedloop session. The per-item sibling of the v1 batch tag apply, which refuses the whole batch when any id is missing from the organization. This tags the ids that resolved and reports the rest `artifacts_not_found`. A `tagId` outside the caller's organization fails every item identically, so it stays a 404 envelope. Returns 200 with one result per DISTINCT requested id, in the order the caller first named it, even when some items fail. Read each item's own `status` and `code`; treat an unrecognized `code` as a generic failure for that item.

tagId.description: The tag to apply. Must belong to the caller's organization.

entityType.description: Batch apply is artifact-only — the write is `tag_artifacts` rows.

entityIds.description: Artifact UUIDs to tag. Duplicates are counted once, and re-applying an existing tag is a no-op that still reports 200 for that id.

200.description: One result per requested artifact. A tagged id carries `status` 200; an id outside the caller's organization carries `artifacts_not_found` at 404.

400.description: Invalid request body: an empty set, more than 500 ids, a malformed UUID, or an `entityType` other than `ARTIFACT`.

401.description: No usable credential: the request carried neither a valid `sk_live_` API key nor a signed-in Closedloop session.

403.description: Either the API key lacks the `write` scope, or — on the session path — the request names an organization the caller is not a member of, which carries `code` `org_forbidden` and is fixed by re-authenticating rather than by a permission change.

404.description: The tag is absent or outside the caller's organization. Nothing was tagged.

post.summary: Remove one tag from many artifacts
post.description: Accepts an API key with `write` scope, or a signed-in Closedloop session. The whole batch is refused when the tag is absent from the caller's organization or any requested artifact cannot be resolved there. Returns 200 with one result per DISTINCT requested id, in the order the caller first named it. Each applied result distinguishes a membership that was `removed` from one that was `not_present`; an absent membership is an idempotent success.

tagId.description: The tag to remove. Must belong to the caller's organization.

entityType.description: Batch removal is artifact-only — the write deletes `tag_artifacts` rows.

entityIds.description: Artifact UUIDs to untag. Duplicates are counted once, and removing a tag that is not present is a no-op that reports 200 with outcome `not_present` for that id.

200.description: One result per requested artifact. Every result carries `status` 200 and an outcome of `removed` or `not_present`; `not_present` is an idempotent success.

400.description: Invalid request body: an empty set, more than 500 ids, a malformed UUID, or an `entityType` other than `ARTIFACT`.

403.description: Either the API key lacks the `write` scope, or — on the session path — the request names an organization the caller is not a member of, which carries `code` `org_forbidden` and is fixed by re-authenticating rather than by a permission change.

get.description:
Search across the organization. Provide `q` (a free-text query, 2–200 characters), or `tagId` (a tag UUID) to scope results to items carrying that tag. `q` is required unless `tagId` is supplied. The two are **not** mutually exclusive: sending both is accepted, and `tagId` wins — the tag branch runs and `q` is ignored without being validated, so a `q` that would otherwise be rejected as too short or too long still succeeds alongside a `tagId`. When `tagId` is supplied, `tagId`/`tagName` are echoed on the response. Requires the `read` scope.

This endpoint returns **one of two response shapes**, and the request selects which:

- **Documents-and-projects search** (`GlobalSearchResponse`) — a substring search over documents and projects. This is the shape you get for a plain `?q=…` or `?tagId=…` request.
- **Unified search** (`UnifiedSearchResponse`) — a heterogeneous ranked list over the whole corpus (documents, projects, sessions, branches, pull requests, comments, agent components; session transcripts match only for an organization opted into transcript search). The response carries `results`/`nextCursor` instead of `documents`/`projects`.

`tagId` takes precedence over everything below: a request carrying a **non-empty** `tagId` always returns `GlobalSearchResponse`, and any unified param sent alongside it is ignored (`?tagId=<uuid>&cursor=…` does **not** page). The value is trimmed first, so an empty or whitespace-only `tagId` (`?tagId=`, `?tagId=%20`) is treated as absent rather than validated — it does not take precedence and it is not rejected as a malformed UUID; the request falls through to the `q` path (`?tagId=&mode=prefix&q=auth` returns `UnifiedSearchResponse`, and `?tagId=` on its own is a 400 `q is required`). Otherwise the unified shape is returned when **either** of these holds, so a client that only handles `GlobalSearchResponse` must avoid both:

1. Any of `mode`, `types`, `since`, `until`, or `cursor` is present on the request (`limit` alone does not switch shapes).
2. `q` carries an inline query-language filter that the parser ACCEPTS — an `@owner` mention, or a `type:`/`status:`/`priority:`/`project:`/`updated:` token with a valid value (e.g. `?q=auth type:loop`). A filter the parser rejects (`?q=auth type:widget`) is not applied and does not switch shapes, and neither does an unknown key (`?q=auth foo:bar`), which is just free text. A bare `q` with no filter token keeps the documents-and-projects shape.

**Exact ID/slug hits bypass the filters.** On the unified path, the first bare `q` token that looks like an entity UUID or slug (`FEA-42`) is lifted out of the free text and resolved by a separate exact-lookup query, whose match is prepended to `results` ahead of the ranked full-text hits (de-duplicated if the same record also matched the text scan). That lane is scoped by organization and by `types` only. `since`, `until`, and the inline `@owner`/`project:`/`status:`/`priority:`/`updated:` predicates are applied to the full-text lane alone and are **not** applied to it — so an exact hit can be returned even when it falls outside the requested date window or filter set, including when those filters match nothing else. Exact hits are emitted on the first page only (no `cursor`); on later pages the record is excluded from the full-text scan rather than repeated. Every hit is re-authorized individually regardless of lane, so this never widens what a caller may see.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Free-text query (2–200 characters). Required unless `tagId` is provided, and ignored — not even length-validated — when `tagId` is also present.

May carry inline query-language filters: an `@handle` owner mention, or a token whose key is one of `type`, `status`, `priority`, `project`, `updated` (`type:loop`, `status:TODO`, `priority>=HIGH`, `project:acme`, `updated>7d`). A token with any other key (`foo:bar`) is ordinary free text, not a filter. An accepted `type:` filter unions into the same corpus `types` predicate as the `types` query param, so it scopes **both** lanes — including an exact ID/slug hit, which `q` may also carry (`?q=FEA-42 type:project` does not return a `FEA-42` document). The other accepted filters — `@owner`, `project:`, `status:`, `priority:`, `updated:` — narrow the ranked full-text lane only and are **not** applied to an exact hit (see the endpoint description).

What happens to a filter the parser rejects (`type:widget`, `updated:notadate`) depends on which path the request is on. On the unified path it is a 400. On a documents-and-projects request it is neither applied nor reported — and because that path substring-matches the raw `q` as written, without stripping filter tokens, the rejected token is matched literally.

parameters.name: tagId
parameters.description: Restrict results to items carrying this tag (UUID). Not mutually exclusive with `q` — both may be sent, and `tagId` wins: the tag branch runs and `q` is ignored entirely (see the endpoint description). A **non-empty** value that is not a valid UUID is rejected with a 400 (`tagId must be a valid UUID`). The value is trimmed first, so an empty or whitespace-only `tagId` (`?tagId=`, `?tagId=%20`) is treated as absent instead: it is not validated, does not take precedence over `q`, and the request falls through to the `q` path.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Unified search only — selects the query mode. Present at all, this switches the response to `UnifiedSearchResponse`. Defaults to `fulltext` when omitted from an otherwise-unified request; any other value is rejected with a 400.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Unified search only — restrict results to these entity kinds. **Repeated**, not comma-joined: `?types=document&types=loop`. Present at all, this switches the response to `UnifiedSearchResponse`. Any value outside the supported corpus is rejected with a 400 (`Unsupported types value: <value>`), never silently dropped. Unions with any inline `type:` filter in `q`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Unified search only — restrict the ranked full-text lane to entities updated at or after this ISO-8601 date/date-time. Present at all, this switches the response to `UnifiedSearchResponse`. An unparseable value is rejected with a 400. Does **not** constrain an exact ID/slug hit, which is resolved by a separate lane and prepended regardless of this bound (see the endpoint description).

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Unified search only — restrict the ranked full-text lane to entities updated at or before this ISO-8601 date/date-time. Present at all, this switches the response to `UnifiedSearchResponse`. An unparseable value is rejected with a 400. Does **not** constrain an exact ID/slug hit, which is resolved by a separate lane and prepended regardless of this bound (see the endpoint description).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Unified search only — page size, defaulting to 25. Unlike the other unified params this does NOT by itself switch the response shape: it is ignored on a documents-and-projects request. An out-of-range or non-numeric value is clamped to `[1, 100]` (or the default) rather than rejected. It budgets the ranked full-text lane only — exact ID/slug hits are prepended outside that budget, so `results` can exceed `limit` on the first page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Unified search only — the opaque `nextCursor` from a previous `UnifiedSearchResponse`, to fetch the next page. Present at all, this switches the response to `UnifiedSearchResponse`. An undecodable cursor degrades to the first page rather than erroring.

200.description: Search results. The `data` shape depends on the request: `GlobalSearchResponse` for a plain `q`/`tagId` search, or `UnifiedSearchResponse` when the request takes the unified path (see the endpoint description).

data.description: A `GlobalSearchResponse` (documents + projects) by default, or a `UnifiedSearchResponse` (ranked heterogeneous `results` + `nextCursor`) when — absent a `tagId`, which always wins — any of `mode`, `types`, `since`, `until`, or `cursor` is present, or `q` carries an inline query-language filter the parser accepts.

400.description: `q` is required (or missing when `tagId` is absent), too short/long, or `tagId` is not a valid UUID. On the unified path also: an unsupported `types` value, an unrecognized `mode`, an unparseable `since`/`until`, or a malformed inline filter token in `q`.

403.description: Missing or insufficient `read` scope.

The default `quality=all` view returns every session; pass `quality=substantive` to hide idle (0 turns, 0 tokens, and 0 tool uses) sessions, or `quality=idle` to return only those idle sessions. Requires the `read` scope.

post.summary: Create an agent session
post.description: Creates a session on a compute target in the caller's organization, or returns the existing one unchanged. IDEMPOTENT on `(computeTargetId, externalSessionId)`: a retry returns the already-present row with `created: false` rather than minting a second session, so this endpoint can safely pre-register a run the desktop will later sync. Requires the `write` scope.

computeTargetId.description: The compute target the session runs on. Must belong to the caller's organization, or the request returns `400`.

externalSessionId.description: Caller-owned identity of the run on that compute target. Together with `computeTargetId` this is the same unique key the desktop sync upserts on, which is what makes a retry idempotent and lets a later desktop sync of the same run land on this row. Deliberately unbounded on the wire: an over-long value is projected down at the column, exactly as the desktop sync path projects it.

status.description: Session lifecycle state. Only these three LIFECYCLE values are accepted; the display-only spellings the read side projects (`waiting`, `unknown`, `stale`) are rejected with `400` rather than folded, so a write can never store a state the caller did not ask for.

projectId.description: Tri-state: omit the key to leave the stored value alone, send `null` to clear the assignment, or send a UUID to assign it. The UUID is verified against the caller's organization before it is written.

ownerUserId.description: Tri-state: omit the key to leave the stored value alone, send `null` to clear the assignment, or send a UUID to assign it. The UUID is verified against the caller's organization before it is written.

harness.description: Harness that produced the run, e.g. `claude`.

startedAt.description: ISO-8601. Defaults to the server clock.

200.description: The created session, or the already-present one when `created` is `false`.

400.description: Invalid request body, or a `computeTargetId`, `projectId` or `ownerUserId` outside the caller's organization.

403.description: The API key lacks the `write` scope.

The read is scoped to the authenticated organization, so a session belonging to another organization returns `404` rather than `403`. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.description: Agent-session UUID (the `id` returned by `GET /agent-sessions`).

patch.description: Updates the name, lifecycle status, project, or owner of one session in the caller's organization. `projectId` and `ownerUserId` are tri-state — omit to leave alone, `null` to clear, a UUID to assign. A session in another organization returns `404` rather than `403`. Note that `status` is rewritten by the desktop sync's update arm on the next sync of the same run; `name` is not, because a rename is stored apart from the collector-derived name. Renaming additionally requires that the caller OWN the session or hold an admin role in the organization — any other member gets `403` — and must be sent on its own, since a body pairing `name` with `status`, `projectId`, or `ownerUserId` is rejected with `400` rather than half-applied. Requires the `write` scope.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Agent-session UUID (the `id` returned by `GET /agent-sessions`).

name.description: The user-authored session name. Stored apart from the collector-derived name so a rename survives the next desktop sync, and bounded at 200 characters because the desktop sync payload carries the same field under that ceiling. Authorized to the session's owner or an organization admin, and must be sent WITHOUT `status`, `projectId`, or `ownerUserId`.

status.description: Session lifecycle state. Only these three LIFECYCLE values are accepted; the display-only spellings the read side projects (`waiting`, `unknown`, `stale`) are rejected with `400` rather than folded, so a write can never store a state the caller did not ask for.

projectId.description: Tri-state: omit the key to leave the stored value alone, send `null` to clear the assignment, or send a UUID to assign it. The UUID is verified against the caller's organization before it is written.

ownerUserId.description: Tri-state: omit the key to leave the stored value alone, send `null` to clear the assignment, or send a UUID to assign it. The UUID is verified against the caller's organization before it is written.

priority.description: Tri-state: omit the key to leave the stored value alone, send `null` to clear the priority, or send a value to set it. Must be sent WITHOUT `name`, `status`, `projectId`, or `ownerUserId`.

expectedPriority.description: Optional optimistic guard for `priority`, and only valid alongside it. The write is refused with `409` and code `stale_priority` unless the stored priority still equals this value, where `null` asserts that the session holds no priority. A `priority` the session already holds is never refused, so a retried write succeeds. Omit the key for last-write-wins.

expectedName.description: Optional optimistic guard for `name`, and only valid alongside it. Compared with the name the session currently shows. The write is refused with `409` and code `stale_name` unless that name still equals this value. A `name` the session already shows is never refused, so a retried write succeeds. Omit the key for last-write-wins.

expectedStatus.description: Optional optimistic guard for `status`, and only valid alongside it. The write is refused with `409` and code `stale_status` unless the stored status still equals this value. A `status` the session already holds is never refused, so a retried write succeeds. Omit the key for last-write-wins.

expectedProjectId.description: Optional optimistic guard for `projectId`, and only valid alongside it. The write is refused with `409` and code `stale_project_id` unless the stored project still equals this value, where `null` asserts that the session is in no project. A `projectId` the session already holds is never refused, so a retried write succeeds. Omit the key for last-write-wins.

expectedOwnerUserId.description: Optional optimistic guard for `ownerUserId`, and only valid alongside it. The write is refused with `409` and code `stale_owner_user_id` unless the stored owner still equals this value, where `null` asserts that the session has no owner. An `ownerUserId` the session already holds is never refused, so a retried write succeeds. Omit the key for last-write-wins.

surface.description: Optional provenance for the priority-change analytics event, read only alongside `priority`. Never required for the write: an API-key caller is not attributed, a value outside this enum that this build has not heard of is dropped and the write still commits, and `bulk` is rejected with 400 because a single-session route cannot have originated a bulk write.

200.description: The updated session in the list projection.

400.description: Invalid request body, a `projectId` / `ownerUserId` outside the caller's organization, a body that pairs `name` or `priority` with one of the other fields, or an `expected*` guard sent without the field it guards. `unsupported_field`: the body names a session field this operation does not write, such as a collector-measured value or `tags`. `details.unsupportedFields` lists those keys and `details.writableFields` lists the body keys that write a session field; when a refused key is the read name of a writable field (`project`, `assignee`), `details.useFields` maps it to the body key to send (`projectId`, `ownerUserId`). Nothing was written. A key that is not a session field at all is stripped rather than refused, so a newer client's extra field does not fail the request.

403.description: The API key lacks the `write` scope, or a rename was attempted by a caller who neither owns the session nor holds an organization admin role. A refused rename carries `field_forbidden` and `details.forbiddenFields` of `["name"]`.

404.description: No agent session with that ID in the caller's organization. Carries `artifacts_not_found`.

409.description: A guard is stale: `stale_priority`, `stale_name`, `stale_status`, `stale_project_id`, or `stale_owner_user_id`, for the `expected*` field whose stored value equals neither the expected value nor the value being written. `details` lists each stale field. Nothing was written.

413.description: Request body over the 4 KiB cap this operation enforces.

get.summary: Page an agent session's event stream
get.description: Returns one keyset page of the session's raw event stream, oldest first, in the same `(createdAt, externalEventId)` order as the `events` prefix on `GET /agent-sessions/{id}`. That prefix stops at the detail read's row ceiling (`eventsTruncated`); this endpoint is how a client reaches the events past it, one page at a time. Replay `nextCursor` verbatim as the next request's `cursor` — its absence means the page you hold is the last one. The read is scoped to the authenticated organization, so a session belonging to another organization returns `404` rather than `403`. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Agent-session UUID (the `id` returned by `GET /agent-sessions`).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque `nextCursor` from a prior page of this endpoint. Omit to start from the first event. A value this endpoint could not have minted is a `400`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Events per page. Clamped into 1..2000 rather than rejected, so an out-of-range value returns a bounded page; a present-but-blank `limit=` is a `400`.

200.description: One page of the session's events.

400.description: Invalid query parameters — a `cursor` this endpoint did not mint, or a blank `limit`.

403.description: The API key lacks the `read` scope.

404.description: No agent session with that id exists in the authenticated organization.

post.summary: Bulk-assign a project or owner to agent sessions
post.description: Assigns one field — `project` or `owner` — across a set of sessions. ALL-OR-NOTHING: every ID is authorized individually against the caller's organization and the written row count is compared against the requested ID count inside a transaction, so a set containing an ID that is absent or outside the organization is refused whole with `404` and nothing is written. `assignedCount` therefore always equals the number of distinct IDs sent and can never report a partial application. Requires the `write` scope.

sessionIds.description: Sessions to assign. An empty array or more than 500 IDs is rejected with `400` rather than truncated, because silently assigning a prefix would report a bulk edit that only partly happened. Duplicates are counted once.

value.description: The project or user UUID to assign, verified against the caller's organization. `null` unassigns.

400.description: Invalid request body (empty set, over 500 IDs, malformed UUID), or a target project or owner outside the caller's organization.

403.description: The API key lacks the `write` scope.

404.description: At least one ID is absent or outside the caller's organization. Nothing was written.

post.summary: Bulk-assign a project or owner to agent sessions with per-item results
post.description: Accepts an API key with `write` scope, or a signed-in Closedloop session. Still ALL-OR-NOTHING, exactly like `POST /agent-sessions/bulk-assign`: a set containing an id that is absent or outside the caller's organization writes NOTHING. What changes is the reporting — instead of a bare 404, the response names the offending ids `artifacts_not_found` (404) and every other id `batch_refused` (424), so a client can say which id cost the batch. Returns 200 with one result per DISTINCT requested id, in the order the caller first named it, even when some items fail. Read each item's own `status` and `code`; treat an unrecognized `code` as a generic failure for that item.

sessionIds.description: Sessions to assign. An empty array or more than 500 ids is rejected with 400 rather than truncated. Duplicates are counted once.

field.description: Which field to assign. `project` writes the session artifact; `owner` writes its session-detail row.

value.description: The project or user id to assign, or `null` to clear the field. A target outside the caller's organization is rejected with 400.

200.description: Either every session was assigned, or the batch was refused and each id is labelled: `artifacts_not_found` for the ids that could not be reached, `batch_refused` for the ids that were fine. A refused batch wrote nothing.

400.description: Invalid request body (empty set, over 500 ids, malformed UUID), or a target project or owner outside the caller's organization.

401.description: No usable credential: the request carried neither a valid `sk_live_` API key nor a signed-in Closedloop session.

403.description: Either the API key lacks the `write` scope, or — on the session path — the request names an organization the caller is not a member of, which carries `code` `org_forbidden` and is fixed by re-authenticating rather than by a permission change.

post.summary: Batch set artifact favorites with per-item results
post.description: Sets favorite state for eligible artifacts and reports unresolved ids individually. Requires the write scope for API keys.

200.description: One per-item result for each distinct requested id, with a transactionId receipt.

400.description: Invalid request body; nothing was written.

401.description: No valid API key or signed-in session.

403.description: The API key lacks the `write` scope, or the signed-in caller is not a member of the requested organization (`org_forbidden`).

get.description: Aggregates the organization's agent sessions into a usage summary: session and token totals, the three-way cost split (subscription-covered, confirmed metered, and unclassified spend), and breakdowns by Owner (the session's assignee), model, harness, and repository. Accepts the same filters as `GET /agent-sessions` and covers exactly the population that endpoint lists for the same query, so the totals reconcile against the list. Like the list, the date window is an ACTIVITY window on `lastActivityAt`. Pass `comparison=prior` to also receive server-computed period-over-period movement. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.name: comparison
parameters.description: Opt in to server-computed period-over-period movement, returned in `comparison`. `prior` measures against a window one full period back, so the two slices sit at the same phase of the period — while the requested period is still running that window is cut to the span it has ELAPSED, so the two are equal-length and equal-phase but NOT adjacent (see `AgentSessionUsageComparison`). Requires BOTH `startDate` and `endDate`; with either missing there is no window to step back from and no `comparison` is returned. Accepted only on this endpoint — the list, analytics, and export reads reject it rather than accepting and dropping it.

200.description: The usage summary for the matched sessions.

400.description: Invalid query parameters (e.g. `viewerScope=team` with no `teamId`, or `teamId` alongside a non-`team` `viewerScope`). A refused `listQuery` also carries `code` (a `list_query_*` reason) and `details`.

403.description: The API key lacks the `read` scope, or the requested team scope is not authorized.

get.summary: Count agent sessions by displayed status
get.description: Returns how many agent sessions each DISPLAYED status holds for one filter set, in a single request that builds no per-session projection. Accepts the same filters as `GET /agent-sessions` EXCEPT `status` and `statuses`, which are REJECTED with a 400 rather than accepted and ignored: this endpoint answers for every status at once, so a status selection would zero every bucket the caller did not name. It also takes no `limit`, `offset`, `sortBy`, `sortDir` or `sorts` - there are no rows to page or order, and on the list `limit` bounds the rows returned rather than the work done to build them. Like the list, the date window is an ACTIVITY window on `lastActivityAt`, and the counts cover the population `GET /agent-sessions` lists for the same query - with one bounded exception under a cost-bucket filter, described on `total`. Requires the `read` scope.

200.description: The per-status counts for the matched sessions.

400.description: Invalid query parameters - including `status` or `statuses`, which this endpoint does not accept, and `viewerScope=team` with no `teamId`. A refused `listQuery` also carries `code` (a `list_query_*` reason) and `details`.

403.description: The API key lacks the `read` scope, or the requested team scope is not authorized.

get.description: Breaks the organization's agent sessions down by tool, agent type, repository, and project. Accepts the same filters as `GET /agent-sessions`, with one deliberate difference: the date window here is a session START window on the session's start time, not the list's and usage summary's `lastActivityAt` activity window — so the same `startDate`/`endDate` can match a different set of sessions than the list does. This read has NO server-side population cap, and no `limit` parameter to supply — the query schema is strict, so a caller cannot voluntarily bound the population even if they want to. With no `startDate`/`endDate` it pages every session in the organization into memory, holding two full accumulations of the result at once, and each matched session's event stream is itself fetched unbounded — unlike the single-session detail read, which caps events at 10,000. The failure mode is MEMORY, not latency: a large enough request can exhaust the API process's heap and fail the request outright rather than merely running slowly, and a request timeout does not bound it. Always send a `startDate`/`endDate` window. Requires the `read` scope.

200.description: The analytics breakdowns for the matched sessions.

400.description: Invalid query parameters (e.g. `viewerScope=team` with no `teamId`, or `teamId` alongside a non-`team` `viewerScope`). A refused `listQuery` also carries `code` (a `list_query_*` reason) and `details`.

403.description: The API key lacks the `read` scope, or the requested team scope is not authorized.

delete.description: Deletes an artifact link by UUID, org-scoped to the authenticated organization. Requires the `delete` scope.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Artifact-link UUID.

403.description: The API key lacks the `delete` scope.

500.description: Failed to delete the artifact link.

bearerAuth.description: Authenticate requests using a Closedloop API key. API keys begin with `sk_live_` and are generated in the Closedloop dashboard. Pass the key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...`

sessionAuth.description: A signed-in Closedloop session, which a small number of operations require INSTEAD of an API key. A browser on the Closedloop app is authenticated automatically by its session cookie; any other caller presents the session token as a Bearer token. A `sk_live_` API key is not a credential for an operation that names this scheme.

AgentSessionViewerScope.name: viewerScope
AgentSessionViewerScope.description: Read scope. `team` requires `teamId`. The ORGANIZATION is the real data boundary here, not the team: `self` is the only value enforced server-side as a narrowing (the read is pinned to the authenticated user), and the team-membership check runs only when you ASK for team scope. A caller who is 403'd requesting team X can omit `viewerScope` and still receive team X's sessions under the default organization scope. Treat `team` as a view, not a permission.

AgentSessionTeamId.name: teamId
AgentSessionTeamId.description: Team UUID. Required when `viewerScope=team`. Sending `teamId` with NO `viewerScope` is accepted as a legacy alias and normalizes to `viewerScope=team`; sending it alongside any other `viewerScope` is rejected.

AgentSessionComponentSlug.name: componentSlug
AgentSessionComponentSlug.description: Scope to the canonical component population identified by an agent-component detail route slug. Applied before session facets, totals and pagination. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed; an empty value is rejected. An unrecognized component identity matches no sessions.

AgentSessionUserId.name: userId
AgentSessionUserId.description: Filter to sessions whose Owner (assignee) is this user (UUID). When `userIds` is also sent the result is their intersection: no sessions are returned unless `userId` is in `userIds`.

AgentSessionStatus.name: status
AgentSessionStatus.description: Filter by a single session status. The canonical filter vocabulary this parameter advertises is `active`, `inactive`, `error` — the three persisted lifecycle values a Status facet offers. The schema stays an open string rather than an enum on purpose: the route matches any spelling it is given, so publishing a narrower contract would make a generated client reject a value the server answers. A spelling outside the three falls through to an exact match on the stored status, so the retired `completed` and `abandoned`, and the display-only `waiting`, `stale` and `unknown` retired as filter values by ISS-10629, are no longer recognized and select nothing. What a row READS BACK is derived rather than stored, and need not be one of the three: a spelling the server does not recognize reads `unknown`, and a stored `active` row reads `waiting` while it awaits input or `stale` once silent past the display cutoff. ISS-5592 retired the last aliases, so `running` and `failed` are no longer recognized either and read `unknown` like any other unmodelled spelling — with the same awaiting-input exception the retired pair carries: that projection runs AHEAD of the unrecognized fold and excludes only spellings the fold reads as terminal, so an unrecognized row carrying an awaiting-input marker and no end time reads `waiting`, not `unknown`. For `failed` that is new: it previously resolved to `error`, which IS terminal and blocked the branch, so a `failed` row that would once have read Error can now read Waiting. These read-back spellings are not themselves selectable by the three values above.

AgentSessionQuality.name: quality
AgentSessionQuality.description: `all` (default) returns every session; `substantive` returns only substantive sessions (at least one turn, token, or tool use); `idle` returns only idle sessions (0 turns, 0 tokens, and 0 tool uses).

AgentSessionActivityStartDate.name: startDate
AgentSessionActivityStartDate.description: Lower bound of the activity window. Keeps only sessions whose `lastActivityAt` falls on or after this date — a point-in-time test on the session's latest activity, not a start-date filter and not an interval overlap.

AgentSessionActivityEndDate.name: endDate
AgentSessionActivityEndDate.description: Upper bound of the activity window. Keeps only sessions whose `lastActivityAt` falls on or before this date, so a session that was active inside the window but active again after it is excluded.

AgentSessionStartedStartDate.name: startDate
AgentSessionStartedStartDate.description: Only sessions STARTED on or after this date. Unlike the list and usage reads, analytics windows on the session start time, so a session that started before the window is excluded even if it was active inside it.

AgentSessionStartedEndDate.name: endDate
AgentSessionStartedEndDate.description: Only sessions STARTED on or before this date. Analytics windows on the session start time, not on last activity.

AgentSessionCompletedAfter.name: completedAfter
AgentSessionCompletedAfter.description: Keep only sessions that FINISHED at or after this instant (`sessionEndedAt >= completedAfter`). This is a separate bound from the `startDate`/`endDate` window and composes with it: a session that started before this instant but ended after it is kept. Unlike that window — whose field differs per endpoint — this bound is applied to the session end time on every endpoint that accepts it. A session that is still running has no end time and is therefore always excluded.

AgentSessionStatuses.name: statuses
AgentSessionStatuses.description: Multi-select form of `status`. Repeat the key to select several values (`?statuses=active&statuses=error`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet. This multi-select takes PRECEDENCE over the single-value `status`: when `statuses` is present and non-empty, `status` is ignored outright — it is neither intersected nor unioned with it. So `?status=active&statuses=error` returns every `error` session, not an empty result. Send one or the other, never both. Each item carries the same canonical filter vocabulary — and the same deliberately open string schema — that `status` advertises.

AgentSessionUserIds.name: userIds
AgentSessionUserIds.description: Multi-select form of `userId` — sessions whose Owner (assignee) is any of these users. Repeat the key to select several values (`?userIds=<uuid>&userIds=<uuid>`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet. When `userId` is also sent the result is their intersection: no sessions are returned unless `userId` is in `userIds`.

AgentSessionRepositories.name: repositories
AgentSessionRepositories.description: Repository full names (`owner/repo`). Repeat the key to select several values (`?repositories=acme/api`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet. Matched against the session's own stored repository. That is not always the `repositoryFullName` response field: the response resolves the repository from the session's touched-branch link first and only falls back to the stored value, so a session whose branch provenance names a different repository is matched here on the stored value while the response reports the branch's.

AgentSessionHarnesses.name: harnesses
AgentSessionHarnesses.description: Multi-select form of `harness`. Repeat the key to select several values (`?harnesses=claude&harnesses=codex`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet. Takes precedence over the single-value `harness`, which stays for backward compatibility.

AgentSessionModels.name: models
AgentSessionModels.description: Matches the session's PRIMARY displayed model — the same value the session record reports as `model`, not every model a session's subagents used. Repeat the key to select several values (`?models=<model>&models=<model>`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionAutonomyTiers.name: autonomyTiers
AgentSessionAutonomyTiers.description: Autonomy-tier ids. The canonical ids are `high`, `mixed`, `guided`, and `unknown`; any other id is accepted and then ignored by the server rather than rejected, so no `enum` is published here. Repeat the key to select several values (`?autonomyTiers=high&autonomyTiers=mixed`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionCostBuckets.name: costBuckets
AgentSessionCostBuckets.description: Cost-bucket ids. The canonical ids are `under_1` (≤ $1), `from_1_to_10`, `from_10_to_50`, `from_50`, and `unknown` (the session's cost was never computed); any other id is accepted and then ignored by the server rather than rejected, so no `enum` is published here. Buckets match the session's RECONCILED cost, not the stored cost rollup, so a legacy session whose rollup reads 0 still lands in the bucket its priced events total. Repeat the key to select several values (`?costBuckets=under_1`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionChangePresence.name: changePresence
AgentSessionChangePresence.description: Whether the session produced file changes. The canonical ids are `has_changes` and `no_changes`; any other id is accepted and then ignored by the server rather than rejected, so no `enum` is published here. Repeat the key to select several values (`?changePresence=has_changes`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionPrAssociation.name: prAssociation
AgentSessionPrAssociation.description: Whether the session has an associated pull request. The canonical ids are `has_pr` and `no_pr`; any other id is accepted and then ignored by the server rather than rejected, so no `enum` is published here. Repeat the key to select several values (`?prAssociation=has_pr`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionPriorities.name: priorities
AgentSessionPriorities.description: Session priority. `NONE` selects sessions that hold no priority. Any other value is rejected with `400`. Repeat the key to select several values (`?priorities=HIGH&priorities=NONE`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionProjectIds.name: projectIds
AgentSessionProjectIds.description: Projects a session TOUCHED — sessions that linked a document belonging to one of these projects. This is a DIFFERENT dimension from `projectId`, not another spelling of it: `projectId` matches the session's own artifact parent, which is null for essentially every desktop-synced session, while `projectIds` walks the session-to-document links. Sending both ANDs them. Repeat the key to select several values (`?projectIds=<uuid>&projectIds=<uuid>`). Values OR together inside this facet and AND with every other facet.

AgentSessionSorts.name: sorts
AgentSessionSorts.description: Ordered multi-rule sort. Repeat the key once per rule, in priority order, each `<column>:<asc|desc>` (`?sorts=status:asc&sorts=cost:desc`). EVERY rule is applied: a later rule decides only the ties its predecessors leave open, and the order is finally made total on the session id so pages are deterministic. Columns are the same vocabulary as `sortBy` (`user` and `assignee` both sort by the session's Owner, the assignee) and directions the same as `sortDir`; a malformed entry, an unknown column, or an unknown direction is REJECTED rather than ignored, so a rule you can see is a rule that ran. When `sorts` is present it decides the order outright and the single-rule `sortBy`/`sortDir` pair is ignored — send one or the other, not both. A column repeated in the list has no effect beyond its first appearance.

AgentSessionSearch.name: search
AgentSessionSearch.description: Accepted and then IGNORED. Retained only so already-installed clients that still serialize it are not rejected by validation; there is no server-side search predicate behind it. Sending it does not narrow the result set — do not present it as a filter.

AgentSessionListQuery.name: listQuery
AgentSessionListQuery.description: The list's filters and sorts as one JSON expression: `{"version":1,"filters":[...],"sorts":[...]}`. Clauses AND together; the values inside one `isAnyOf` clause OR together. Operators are `isAnyOf`, `isBetween`, `isEmpty` and `isNotEmpty`; each field serves the operators its legacy parameter supports. The server translates the expression to the equivalent individual parameters, so it selects and orders exactly what those parameters would. A `lastActivity` `isBetween` clause becomes `startDate`/`endDate`, so it windows on `lastActivityAt` on `GET /agent-sessions`, `/agent-sessions/usage` and `/agent-sessions/export`, and on the session start time on `/agent-sessions/analytics`, as those parameters do there. Of this endpoint family's shared filter and sort parameters, only `viewerScope`, `teamId`, `userId`, `search` and `projectId` may be sent with it on every endpoint, plus `limit` and `offset` on `GET /agent-sessions` only; any other shared filter or sort parameter returns 400. Parameters that belong to one endpoint only, such as `comparison` and `attribution` on `/agent-sessions/usage`, are unaffected. `sorts` is accepted only on `GET /agent-sessions`. A refused expression returns 400 with `code` set to a `list_query_*` reason and `details` naming the `field` and `operator` involved, when there is one.

BatchDocumentSelection.description: A batch selection defined by a server-resolved QUERY instead of an id list (ISS-9579). The server resolves the predicate inside the mutation, so the set an action operates on is never a list the client sent. Exactly one of `documentIds` and `selection` may be sent. A selection resolving to more than 500 artifacts is REFUSED with `code: "selection_too_large"` plus `details.resolvedTotal` and `details.limit`; it is never truncated.

excludedIds.description: Rows the reader deselected inside a select-all. Narrows the resolved set; it can never widen it.

BatchDocumentSelectionQuery.description: The `GET /documents` filter vocabulary, derived from that endpoint's own schema so the population a write touches cannot drift from the population the reader was looking at. The paging keys (`limit`, `offset`, `includeTotal`) and the custom-field sort keys (`customFieldSortId`, `customFieldSortDir`) are omitted deliberately: accepting a page bound would let a caller hand the server a narrowed window and have the write call itself "all results".

unassignedProject.description: Select only project-less documents. A JSON body may send a real boolean; the `"true"`/`"false"` spelling the list endpoint's query string uses is accepted too.

includeArchivedProjects.description: Include documents in archived projects. Same two spellings as `unassignedProject`.

recencyDays.description: Recency window in days over `updatedAt`. `"all"` opts out of the window entirely.

search.description: Free-text narrowing on title and slug, executed over the whole matching population. A blank or whitespace-only term is rejected rather than treated as no search.

status.description: Lifecycle statuses to narrow to, matched as `IN`. The union of both vocabularies, and NOT narrowed by `type`.

oneOf.description: The same array, JSON-encoded: the spelling the list endpoint's query string uses.

customFieldFilters.description: Custom-field facets to narrow by. A JSON body may send the array directly.

values.description: Required for `isAnyOf` and ignored by the other operators. The field's stored type decides how each operand is parsed, which is why it is not required here.

DocumentType.description: The type of document artifact. PRD = Product Requirements Document, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN = implementation plan, TEMPLATE = reusable template, FEATURE = feature specification, DOC = evergreen document.

DocumentTypeInput.description: The accepted document-type input on requests. Supersets the persisted `DocumentType` with the `ISSUE` alias: the product renamed Features to Issues in the UI, so a caller may pass `ISSUE` and it is normalized to the persisted `FEATURE` type. `ISSUE` never persists and never appears in responses (response `type` fields use `DocumentType`), so `type=ISSUE` and `type=FEATURE` both resolve to the same FEATURE-typed artifacts.

DocumentStatus.description: The authoring lifecycle status of a document (PRD, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, TEMPLATE, DOC). FEATURE artifacts use `IssueStatus` instead.

IssueStatus.description: The delivery lifecycle status of a Feature (`type=FEATURE`). Distinct from `DocumentStatus`, which applies to the authoring document types (PRD, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN, TEMPLATE, DOC). Omitting `status` on `POST /documents` for a Feature yields `BACKLOG` (the subtype fallback applied by `fallbackStatusForSubtype`), regardless of caller. `TRIAGE` is NOT an omitted-status default: agent workflows land in `TRIAGE` only because they send it explicitly. Every value, including `TRIAGE`, is selectable by any caller.

allowedStatuses.description: Status values accepted for this document artifact's subtype.

expectedStatusField.description: Field name for the single-document stale-write guard.

expectedStatusByIdField.description: Field name for the batch stale-write guard.

permissions.description: Whether the credential making this request may perform each status write. Resolved only by the artifact detail reads, which hold your credential; omitted entirely — never null — by every other producer of this object. Absence therefore means "not resolved here", never "denied": a client that sees no `permissions` should attempt the write, which the route authorizes independently either way. A display affordance, never the security boundary.

DocumentStatusMutationPermissions.description: Read-vs-write capability for each status write, keyed by operation.

single.description: Whether this credential may set one artifact's status via `PUT /documents/{id}`. Requires an API key with `write` scope.

bulk.description: Whether this credential may set a selection's status via `POST /documents/batch-update-status`. Requires an API key with `write` scope.

avatarUrl.description: URL of the user's avatar image.

organizationId.description: ID of the organization that owns this document.

projectId.description: ID of the project this document belongs to, if any.

fileName.description: Optional file name associated with the document.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the document. A FEATURE artifact carries a Features-vocabulary value (`IssueStatus`, e.g. TRIAGE); every other type carries a Documents-vocabulary value (`DocumentStatus`, e.g. DRAFT).

dueDate.description: Due date for the document, if set.

latestVersion.description: The latest version number of the document.

createdById.description: ID of the user who created the document.

createdBy.description: Summary of the original artifact creator. Null when the creator record is unavailable.

assigneeId.description: ID of the user assigned to this document.

assignee.description: The user assigned to this document.

approverId.description: ID of the user who is the designated approver.

approver.description: The user designated to approve this document.

templateForType.description: When this document is a template, specifies which document type it is a template for.

sortOrder.description: Numeric sort position within a list.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the document was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the document was last updated.

fullName.description: Full repository name in owner/repo format.

role.description: Role of this repository in the artifact.

position.description: Zero-based position ordering of this repository entry.

repositories.description: List of repository entries in this snapshot.

source.description: How this snapshot was populated. `loop_selection` and `branch_link` mean the primary repository was observed; `project_defaults`, `parent_artifact` and `legacy` mean it was guessed or copied and must not be read as a measurement.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was created.

fullName.description: Full repository name in owner/repo format.

branch.description: Optional branch name to pin for this repository. Omit or set to null to leave the branch unpinned.

DocumentRepositorySelection.description: Repository selection to snapshot onto the document at create time. When omitted, the document inherits the source artifact's repository snapshot when `sourceId` is set and that parent snapshot is non-empty; otherwise it falls back to the project's default repositories.

additional.description: Optional additional repositories for the document (up to 5).

LinkType.description: The type of directional relationship between two artifacts. PRODUCES = source artifact generated or produced the target, BLOCKS = source is blocking the target, RELATES_TO = general relationship.

id.description: Unique identifier for the artifact link.

organizationId.description: ID of the organization that owns this link.

sourceId.description: ID of the source artifact in the relationship.

targetId.description: ID of the target artifact in the relationship.

metadata.description: Optional JSON metadata attached to the link.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the link was created.

id.description: Unique identifier for the comment thread.

organizationId.description: ID of the organization that owns this thread.

source.description: The system that originated this thread. NATIVE = Closedloop native, LIVEBLOCKS = Liveblocks collaborative editing, GITHUB = GitHub PR comment projection.

externalId.description: External system identifier for this thread.

artifactId.description: ID of the artifact this thread is attached to.

metadata.description: Optional JSON metadata for the thread.

createdAtVersion.description: Document version number at which this thread was created.

resolvedAt.description: Timestamp when the thread was resolved.

resolvedById.description: ID of the user who resolved the thread.

createdById.description: ID of the user who created the thread.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the thread was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the thread was last updated.

threadId.description: ID of the thread this comment belongs to.

TagListPage.description: Paged list envelope returned by `GET /tags?includeTotal=true` (ISS-7461). The requested page of tags plus a real server-side `total` counted over the same filter, so a paging client can state an honest total without inferring it from the page length. Narrower than `DocumentListPage`, which also reports the `limit`/`offset` it applied after CLAMPING — this endpoint REJECTS an out-of-range bound instead of clamping it, so the caller already knows the window it asked for.

items.description: The requested page of tags, in the same order (by name) the bare-array response returns.

total.description: Real count of every tag matching the filter, counted server-side independently of `limit`/`offset`. Never derived from `items.length`.

hasMore.description: True when tags matching the filter exist beyond this page.

DocumentListPage.description: Paged list envelope returned by `GET /documents?includeTotal=true` (ISS-4576). The requested page of documents plus a real server-side `total` counted over the same filter, so a paging client can state an honest "showing X-Y of N" without inferring the total from the page length.

items.description: The requested page of documents, in the same order the bare-array response returns.

total.description: Real count of every document matching the filter, counted server-side independently of `limit`/`offset`. Never derived from `items.length`.

limit.description: Effective page size the server applied after clamping, or `null` when the caller requested no bound (the whole matching set is in `items`).

offset.description: Effective zero-based offset the server applied after clamping.

hasMore.description: True when documents matching the filter exist beyond this page.

status.description: Status of the document. Uses the Documents or Features vocabulary depending on `type`.

documents.description: Matching documents, capped at 25 (the same cap applies to a `?tagId=` search). This shape carries no `hasMore`, `nextCursor`, or `offset`, so a caller that receives 25 cannot tell whether more matched — use the unified path and its `nextCursor` to page the full corpus.

projects.description: Matching projects, capped at 25 independently of `documents`. As with `documents`, this shape carries no continuation metadata — page via the unified path.

tagId.description: Present when the search was scoped to a tag via `?tagId=`.

tagName.description: Name of the scoped tag, when `tagId` is set.

SearchMode.description: Query mode for the unified search path. `fulltext` (the default) is phrase/operator-aware; `prefix` is typeahead — the trailing token matches as a prefix so a partially-typed word still hits.

SearchEntityType.description:
One entity kind in the unified-search corpus. Also the accepted vocabulary for the `types` query param — a value outside this set is rejected with a 400, never silently dropped.

`agent_session` is accepted for every organization but only *matches* for one that has opted into transcript search: session transcripts are privacy-sensitive, so an opted-out org gets an empty session result rather than an error.

SearchHit.description: One heterogeneous, ranked hit in a `UnifiedSearchResponse`. `entityType` discriminates the kind; the route fields are optional because a hit that lacks the data to build an in-app route degrades to a non-link row rather than a broken one.

snippet.description: Highlighted excerpt around the match, or a plain title fallback.

rank.description: Relevance score; higher is more relevant.

updatedAt.description: The source entity's own last-updated timestamp.

deepLink.description: Org-relative UUID-only locator (e.g. `/documents/<id>`). Best-effort: prefer building the route from the fields below, which resolve the real app path.

slug.description: The entity's URL handle, when it has one (documents route by slug; agent components by their `${kind}::${key}` handle).

entitySubtype.description: A document hit's `type` (used to pick the route prefix), or — for a comment hit — the TYPE of the artifact it is anchored on.

teamId.description: A project hit's owning team, for the team-scoped project route.

anchorEntityId.description: The id of a DIFFERENT entity this hit routes to: a `pull_request` routes to its owning branch, a `comment` to the artifact it is anchored on.

UnifiedSearchResponse.description: The unified full-text search response — a heterogeneous ranked list across the whole corpus. Returned INSTEAD of `GlobalSearchResponse` whenever the request takes the unified path (see the `GET /search` description).

query.description: The free-text portion of the query that was executed, with any inline filter tokens removed. The first bare token that resolves as an entity UUID or slug is also lifted out — into the exact-lookup lane — so it does not appear here either (`?q=FEA-42 auth` echoes `auth`). Empty when no free text remained: the query was all filters, or only that exact ID/slug token (`?q=FEA-42` echoes `""`).

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page — pass it back as `cursor`. `null` when the result set is drained.

AgentSessionListItem.description: One agent session row. This documents the stable core fields; the endpoint also returns many optional, additive projection fields (git diff stats, phases, activity buckets, linked PRs/artifacts, …) that a client should treat as best-effort.

slug.description: SES-* slug of the backing Session artifact.

status.description: Status of the session, DERIVED at read time rather than served from the stored column — so it is NOT bounded by the canonical filter vocabulary the `status`/`statuses` parameters advertise, whose request schemas stay open strings for version-skewed clients. A stored `active` can come back as `waiting` (awaiting user input on a run that has not ended) or as `stale` (silent past the display staleness cutoff), and a stored value this build does not recognize generally comes back as `unknown` — the awaiting-input derivation runs first, so even an unrecognized row can surface as `waiting`. Where no derivation applies the stored value passes through unchanged, including a retired `completed`/`abandoned` from a not-yet-migrated row. Treat this as an open string rather than a closed vocabulary, and do not assume re-sending a returned value as a filter finds the row that carried it.

harness.description: The agent harness that produced the session (e.g. `claude`, `codex`).

cwd.description: Working directory the session ran in.

repositoryFullName.description: The `owner/repo` the session worked in, if known.

model.description: Primary model used by the session.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the session row was last updated.

lastActivityAt.description: Timestamp of the latest genuine agent activity (the default Sessions sort).

endedAt.description: Timestamp when the session ended, if it has.

estimatedCost.description: Estimated cost of the session in USD.

agentCount.description: Number of distinct agents in the session.

toolUseCount.description: Number of tool calls in the session.

errorCount.description: Number of errors recorded in the session.

baseBranch.description: The base branch the session's work targeted.

sourceArtifactId.description: ID of the artifact that sourced the session, if any.

sourceLoopId.description: ID of the loop that produced the session, if any.

user.description: The user who owns the session. Null when the owner has been deleted.

computeTarget.description: Summary of the compute target that produced the session.

project.description: Summary of the project the session is associated with, if any.

total.description: Total number of sessions matching the filters.

viewerScope.description: The scope the results were read at.

idleCount.description: Number of idle sessions hidden by the `quality=substantive` view (the default `quality=all` view returns every session). Omitted (treated as 0) by producers that do not compute it.

pageInfo.description: Which page this read served. Omitted by producers that predate it. The read is always answered at the `offset` that was requested, so an offset past the last page returns an empty `items` and echoes that same offset.

capability.description: What the producer can do with a paged read.

limit.description: The page size the producer honoured. This route rejects a `limit` above the maximum with a 400 rather than clamping it; another producer of this shape may clamp instead, so treat an echoed size that differs from the one requested as a reason to ignore the echo.

offset.description: The offset the returned rows were taken from.

type.description: Agent type as reported by the harness.

subagentType.description: Subagent type, for a spawned subagent.

task.description: The task the agent was given.

currentTool.description: Tool the agent was last using.

awaitingInputSince.description: When the agent began waiting on user input, if it is.

parentExternalAgentId.description: The spawning agent's identifier, for a subagent.
